tools.description: Full-text search the workspace's notes (Russian + English) — use this when you don't know where something lives. Returns ranked hits with highlighted snippets and each hit's `contentChangedAt` (an unchanged-since bound on that note's text — check it before choosing what to read), plus `attachments`: FILES whose name or path matches (filenames only — file contents aren't indexed yet). `degraded: true` means the NOTE index was incomplete for this call — the attachment arm is never degraded, but it IS capped, so check `attachmentsTruncated`.

workspace.description: Workspace @handle or id. Omit if the token is pinned to a single workspace or your account is a member of exactly one workspace (a personal workspace counts); required otherwise — a member of several workspaces must name one.

tools.name: search_notes

tools.description: Read a note: markdown source, frontmatter, backlinks, outgoing links (`links` = resolved NOTE targets, `unresolved` = dangling refs), `embeds` (the FILES this note shows — read those with read_attachment before concluding you have read the note), tags, `relatedHint` (a few neighbours worth checking), and `contentChangedAt` — an unchanged-since bound on the body's text, `null` on the few notes no writer has stamped — plus, when it is non-null, a plain-language `notice` about how far to trust the BODY's current-state claims. Identify it by `path` or `id`. For a file, use attachment_info / read_attachment instead.

workspace.description: Workspace @handle or id. Omit if the token is pinned to a single workspace or your account is a member of exactly one workspace (a personal workspace counts); required otherwise — a member of several workspaces must name one.

tools.name: read_note

tools.description: Read several notes in one call, by `paths` and/or `ids` (max 100) — use it after search_notes rather than reading hits one at a time. Each note carries `contentChangedAt`, an unchanged-since bound on its text. Returns them in request order; unknown refs land in `missing`; refs past the server byte cap land in `skipped` (follow up with another call); refs that name a FILE land in `attachments` (read those with read_attachment).

workspace.description: Workspace @handle or id. Omit if the token is pinned to a single workspace or your account is a member of exactly one workspace (a personal workspace counts); required otherwise — a member of several workspaces must name one.

tools.name: read_notes

tools.description: Read the WHOLE vault (every live note's path + content + `contentChangedAt`, an unchanged-since bound on its text; stable path order) if it fits your byte budget — ideal for small workspaces instead of many searches. Pass `max_bytes` = what you can afford to load (~4 bytes ≈ 1 token). Files are listed (`attachments`: path, mime, size) but never inlined, so they don't consume the budget. If it doesn't fit, you get `fits: false` with the sizes plus a vault map (per-folder note and file totals + top notes by backlinks/recency, each with its `contentChangedAt`) to guide `read_vault` on a `folder`, `read_notes`, or `search_notes`.

max_bytes.description: Your budget in UTF-8 bytes (~4 bytes ≈ 1 token; server cap 4 MiB).

workspace.description: Workspace @handle or id. Omit if the token is pinned to a single workspace or your account is a member of exactly one workspace (a personal workspace counts); required otherwise — a member of several workspaces must name one.

tools.name: read_vault

tools.description: List the workspace's notes AND files (id, path, kind, size in bytes, updatedAt; `mime` on files), optionally under a folder — the way to see what exists. `kind` is "file" for a note and "attachment" for a file. Set include_folders to also list folders (incl. empty ones); set include_attachments:false to list notes only. Pass `since` (RFC 3339) to get only rows changed after it — use the response's `cursor` as your next `since`. Best-effort feed: a write concurrent with your poll can rarely be missed until its next edit; trashed rows just disappear (deletions aren't reported).

folder.description: Limit to items under this folder path.

since.description: RFC 3339 timestamp; only rows updated strictly after it.

File subjects are ranked on the link graph and tags only — file contents aren't indexed yet.

tools.name: create_folder

tools.description: Create a note or update its ENTIRE markdown body (like a file `write`). By `path`: creates the note if it doesn't exist (the parent folder must already exist — use create_folder first), otherwise updates the existing note. By `id`: updates an existing note (you can't create by id). There is no fragment/patch mode — `content` must be the FULL body; for a TARGETED change use edit_note instead, and to add to the end use append_to_note. On an update, pass `base` (the full body you last read): your body and the current note are compared with that common base, and the resulting changes are merged word by word. Without `base`, your body replaces whatever the note holds now (last writer wins). Returns `created` (true if a new note was made), `mergedWithLiveEdits` (true if the note had changed since `base` and your body was merged with those changes without creating a conflict sibling), `overlappingEdits` (how many of your changes touched text also changed since `base` — at those locations, the note holds text from both sides; if the count is above 0, re-read the note and resolve those overlaps with edit_note) and `conflictSiblingId` (non-null only in a rare fallback when the merge could not run and both versions were kept separately in the original note and a conflict sibling — reconcile them before trashing the sibling). For your next whole-body write, you may reuse the body you just sent as `base` only if `mergedWithLiveEdits` was false and `conflictSiblingId` was null; otherwise re-read the note and use its full body as `base`. Never reuse an older base.

base.description: Optional (overwrite only): the FULL body you last read, used as the common base for a word-by-word merge of your body with the current note. Without `base`, your body replaces whatever the note holds now (last writer wins).

content.description: The FULL markdown body (whole-note write — never a fragment).

id.description: Id of an existing note to overwrite (alternative to path).

path.description: Note path, e.g. Folder/Note.md. The name must end in .md. Created if missing.

workspace.description: Workspace @handle or id. Omit if the token is pinned to a single workspace or your account is a member of exactly one workspace (a personal workspace counts); required otherwise — a member of several workspaces must name one.

tools.description: Replace an exact string in a note (identified by `path` or `id`) — for targeted edits without resending the body. `old_string` must match the note text EXACTLY, whitespace and newlines included, and must be unique unless replace_all is true. `new_string` may be empty (deletion). Whole-note rewrites should use write_note instead.

new_string.description: The replacement text (empty deletes the match).

old_string.description: The exact text to replace (must be non-empty and match exactly).

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence (default false — then old_string must be unique).

tools.name: attachment_info

tools.description: Get a FILE's content (identified by `path` or `id`). Small PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP images come back INLINE and you can see them directly. Everything else — PDFs, documents, big images, SVG/HEIC — comes back as `download.href`: a short-lived URL you fetch with curl — no Authorization header needed, because the URL ITSELF is the credential, so don't paste it anywhere shared (docli.ru must be reachable from where you run it). File CONTENTS are not searchable yet, so this is the way to look inside one.

tools.name: read_attachment

tools.description: Put a FILE into the vault at `path`. Tiny files (≤64 KiB): pass `content_base64`. Anything bigger: pass `total_bytes` and NO content — you get back an upload URL, a chunk size, and a completion URL to drive with curl; re-call with the same `upload_id` to resume or check progress. The parent folder must already exist (create_folder first). Re-uploading identical bytes to the same path returns the existing file instead of a duplicate. The response's `wikilink` is ready to paste into a note with edit_note.

content_base64.description: Base64 of the whole file — inline tier only, ≤64 KiB decoded.

path.description: Destination path incl. filename, e.g. assets/diagram.png. Parent folder must exist. A .md name is refused — notes are created with write_note.

sha256.description: Optional hex digest of the whole file; verified at completion.

total_bytes.description: Total file size; REQUIRED when you omit content_base64.

upload_id.description: Resume/check an upload started earlier (the id from a previous call).

workspace.description: Workspace @handle or id. Omit if the token is pinned to a single workspace or your account is a member of exactly one workspace (a personal workspace counts); required otherwise — a member of several workspaces must name one.
